bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI focused on systems that learn from data and improve over time.
Systems identify patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Used in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: Trains on labeled data to predict outputs (Regression, Classification).
Unsupervised Learning: Trains on unlabeled data to find hidden patterns (Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: Agent learns by interacting with an environment to maximize rewards.
Model Training: Feeding data to a model to learn patterns and minimize prediction errors.
Features and Labels: Input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: Data split for model training and performance evaluation.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Model learns noise too well (overfitting) or is too simple (underfitting).
Linear Regression: Models linear relationships for regression tasks.
Logistic Regression: Predicts class probabilities for classification tasks.
Decision Trees: Non-linear model that splits data based on feature values.
Random Forest: Ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Finds optimal hyperplane to separate data points for classification.
Neural Networks: Brain-inspired models for learning complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: Disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment.
Finance: Fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: Customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: Processing sensor data, decision-making, safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): Language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: Evaluate model performance using separate datasets with metrics like accuracy or MSE.
Cross-Validation: Technique to ensure models generalize well to unseen data.
Hyperparameter Tuning: Optimizing model settings (hyperparameters) for optimal performance.
Data Quality and Quantity: Requires large amounts of accurate data; labeled data collection can be difficult.
Interpretability: Complex models, especially deep learning, are hard to understand.
Bias in Data: Models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Common issues affecting model generalization to new data.
Continuous evolution with advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Increased computational power and datasets will expand ML's role across industries.
ML applications will become more integrated into daily life.
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices will be essential.
